problem.text: Bob wants to climb $8$ stairs. He can climb $1$ or $2$ stairs at a time. How many ways are there for him to climb the $8$ stairs?

steps.title: Where to start: look at Bob's last move
steps.body:
Listing every way to climb $8$ stairs would take a long time, so build the count up from smaller staircases. Let $a_n$ be the number of ways to climb $n$ stairs. Bob's last move is either $1$ stair (from stair $n-1$) or $2$ stairs (from stair $n-2$), and these two groups do not overlap, so
$$a_n = a_{n-1} + a_{n-2}.$$

your_turn.prompt: List all the ways to climb $3$ stairs.

steps.title: Find the starting values and build up
steps.body: There is $1$ way to climb $1$ stair, so $a_1 = 1$. There are $2$ ways to climb $2$ stairs ($1+1$ or $2$), so $a_2 = 2$. Now the rule gives each next value from the two before it.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: Keep going: $a_6 = 8 + 5 = 13$, $a_7 = 13 + 8 = 21$, and $a_8 = 21 + 13 = 34$. These are the Fibonacci numbers. The answer is **$34$**.
